doc.title: Lou Marini interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 15, 2023

title: Steve Martin and King Tut on Saturday Night Live
summary: Marini describes the make-up and the sarcophagus on the day of the King Tut skit.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: Okay. Do you get people, are you tired of people asking you about Steve Martin and King Tut?

No, no. Because you know that was such a crazy day. The guys were all treating me so weird, every time I walked in the dressing room they were tittering and I felt like I was interrupting something. They had bought a stink bomb which they were going to put in the sarcophagus and then they thought they’d all get fired. And then the make-up, they had to apply at like 6:30, they called me into make-up, and it was horrible. It was all my arms and shoulders and my chest and all over my face. It felt so constricting and so weird. And then they told me that I’d have to wear it the whole night because there was so much stuff to do that they weren’t going to be able to take it off and re-apply it between the dress rehearsal and the show. So then I had to get touched up before the show itself. And then I’m in this sarcophagus and I’m crammed in, like wedged in there, and I could see out the little sides. And I’m wearing this super heavy outfit, gold outfit and that thing. And I’m thinking to myself I came to New York to play jazz, what the fuck am I doing. But then I’m looking out and I see my, you know Rubin and Howard Johnson and Cranshaw and the guys, Malone. And I’m thinking I look ridiculous but they really look ridiculous. And then the door opens and I play the solo and it was a live solo, everything was pre-recorded. And then the chick jams me back in, which is not the way we rehearsed it. And suddenly I’m wedging myself back into the sarcoph — that was a bizarre day man. But that’s a classic thing.
